Criterion: Verify that maintenance checklists are available for critical maintenance tasks, such as fuel and oxygen servicing procedures, towing procedures and restrictions, jacking procedures, engine operation during maintenance, lifting procedures, integrated combat turn procedures, etc. Standard: Maintenance checklists are developed in accordance with applicable service's procedures (e.g., 2.4.3, 2.4.3.1, 2.4.3.1.1, 2.4.3.2 of USAF TO 00-5-1, Air Force Technical Order System, COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2) for preparing maintenance publications. Method of Compliance: The maintenance checklists developed are verified by showing traceability from the support analysis, and are verified by the Government. References: JSSG-2000: 3.6.1, 3.6.2 JSSG-2001: 3.1.5 USAF TO 00-5-1, Air Force Technical Order System, 2.4.3, 2.4.3.1, 2.4.3.1.1, 2.4.3.2 COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2 14 CFR 23.1501, 23.1529, 25.1501, 25.1503-25.1533, 25.1529, 25.1541, 25.1543, 25.1557, 25.1563

Standard: Maintenance checklists do not introduce AW hazards to the air vehicle and are derived from the detailed procedures contained in the maintenance publication. Maintenance checklists are IAW MIL-DTL-5096, Checklists paragraphs. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine maintenance checklists to ensure no deviations exist between checklists and procedures within the maintenance publications.
(2) Examine the artifacts that demonstrate contractor certification or contractor validation to ensure the maintenance publications have undergone a quality check for currency and accuracy IAW TO 00-5-3, Contractor Certification Process and Certification Requirements paragraphs for the Air Force; NAVAIR 00-25-604, Contractor Validation Plan and Validation paragraphs for the Navy; and DA PAM 25-40, Validation paragraphs for the Army. Demonstration.
  (1) Perform air vehicle maintainability demonstrations to confirm the maintenance checklists are complete, accurate, do not deviate from procedures within the maintenance publications, and can be performed as written without introducing AW hazards. Maintenance publications will receive updates to address maintenance issues discovered during maintainability demonstrations. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Demonstration.
  (2) Perform all air vehicle maintenance checklist procedures on production-configured hardware using government maintenance personnel to ensure maintenance checklists do not introduce AW hazards.
